propositions: A primary comment-dedup guard (binding_store.is_comment_mapped keyed on comment ID) was inert in production because the comment_ids map in .bridge_state/bindings.json was empty, never populated from feature launch until fix 8d98c298fa8 landed six days later.

The feature's secondary dedup fallback (body-equality skip) silently absorbed traffic while the primary path was inert, masking the defect as partial success rather than total failure and making the degradation appear content-correlated rather than systemic.

Tests covering the dedup path seed invariants into stubs rather than crossing the apply-to-differ seam, so no test could detect that real ACLI responses lack the top-level id field that the primary guard depends on.

Multiple plan-review and code-review criteria had scope boundaries drawn just short of the silent fail-open guard: E4 abstains on external facts, T3 stops at endpoint existence, T5b addresses plans rather than guards.

The invariant violation (comment_ids remaining empty while bindings grew past 2,475 and outbound posts succeeded) persisted in committed production data for the feature's entire operational window with no operator-visible signal.

A production-linked invariant check (comparing successful outbound comment posts against comment_ids growth per pass, emitted via bridge_alerts) would have surfaced the escape immediately and is portable across deployments without CI coupling.
